before.overview: A harder, more direct variation of the standard North Face, sharing the same start and lower pitch but staying direct through steeper crack/corner terrain (5.8) rather than stepping right on the standard 5.6-5.7 line, before rejoining the standard route for the final pitch to the summit.
pro_tips: From the tree ledge atop pitch 1, continue straight up the corner system instead of stepping right onto the standard 5.6-5.7 line.

pitch_detail.notes: Shares the standard North Face's opening crack-to-ledge pitch off the notch, though parties typically belay a bit further right on the ledge to line up for the direct finish above.

The direct ('Directisimo') line: a sustained crack running hands to off-width to chimney size, steeper and more direct than the standard route's step-right option, with one section that breaks briefly onto the face where the crack pinches down partway up.
Gain the arête and follow its exposed crest back up, rejoining the standard North Face's final moves near the summit block.
pitch_detail.anchor: 2-bolt summit anchor (rap chains, shared w/ North Face)

before.rope_note: Single rack to 3 inches, stoppers and slings, on a 70 m rope. Do not rack off the standard North Face's grades: this variation shares the standard route's opening 5.6 crack off the notch, then takes a sustained 5.8 crack that runs hands to off-width to chimney size where the standard line steps right at 5.6-5.7, and rejoins it for a 5.7 arete pitch near the summit. Off the top, single-rope rappels work down either face; the south face is the better choice because ropes tend to snag on the north side.

days.note: Same approach to the col/notch as the standard North Face. Share its first pitch, then break right into a sustained 5.8 crack-to-chimney crux pitch, finishing up an exposed arete pitch to the summit.

itinerary.totalNote: A standard single day (about 9 hrs car-to-car); a bit slower than the easier 5.6 North Face due to the sustained 5.8 offwidth/chimney crux.
